summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with a one-week history of dry heaving and epigastric pain, recurring shortly after a prior hospitalization for similar symptoms. She has a complex surgical history including Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and gastrostomy tube placement due to prior GJ anastomotic ulcer. On admission, she was started on IV fluids, which resolved her symptoms. She remained hemodynamically stable, afebrile, and without leukocytosis. Laboratory results were largely normal, and she tolerated enteral nutrition via G-tube at full strength. Treatment included continuation of lansoprazole and rifaximin, with addition of sucralfate for gastric protection. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue medications and follow up with her specialist.
problems: Unspecified gastritis and gastroduodenitis, without mention of hemorrhage
Personal history of peptic ulcer disease
